sections.h2: Selling a house in Queen Creek, AZ
sections.html:
Queen Creek owners can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept an offer from a cash buyer who needs no mortgage. Homeowners are the norm here: 90.2 percent of occupied homes are lived in by their owners.

  • List with an agent: the house is marketed widely, and you handle showings, buyer repair requests and the wait for loan approval.
  • Sell on your own: you set the price, deal with buyers directly and prepare the deed and affidavit of property value.
  • Cash sale: the buyer pays without a lender, and you compare the offer with the net from a listing after fees and repairs.

If an association governs your street, ask it for its governing documents and any unpaid dues before you accept an offer. A buyer will want them at closing.

The estimated population was 89,770 on July 1, 2025, up 51.4 percent from the 2020 base. The median owner-occupied home was valued at $635,400 for 2020 to 2024, median gross rent was $2,210 and median household income was $141,978. A typical household has 3.21 people, and 30.5 percent of residents are under 18, so your likely buyer is a family.

The mean commute is 31.1 minutes. Be ready to answer questions about drive times to work and to the freeway when you show or describe the house.

Most of Queen Creek is in Maricopa County. The eastern and southern edges reach into Pinal County, and the Ironwood Crossing neighborhood joined the town by annexation in 2018. Your parcel number tells you which county records the deed and which assessor handles the parcel.

Heat is the main force on a house here. Temperatures reach or pass 100 degrees on about 103 days a year, and 11 of those days hit 110 or more. The record high is 119 degrees. Annual precipitation is only about 8.3 inches, mostly from the July to mid-September monsoon. A buyer will check:

  • Air conditioning: the age of the unit and its service history
  • Roof and attic: sustained heat ages roofing materials, and attic ventilation matters
  • Pool equipment, if there is a pool: pumps and decking see heavy use in long summers
  • Grading and gutters: a short, hard monsoon storm can pool water against a foundation

Hard freezes of 28 degrees or lower come only every couple of years, so frozen pipes worry buyers less than in northern Arizona.

sections.h2: Which school district serves the address?
sections.html: Six public school districts serve the town, so the answer depends on the address. Most of the Maricopa County part falls in Queen Creek Unified, with portions in Higley Unified and Chandler Unified. The Pinal County part is split among Florence Unified, J. O. Combs Unified and Apache Junction Unified. Boundaries do not follow town limits, so tell buyers to confirm the assigned school for the exact address with the district.

A buyer can rent a Queen Creek house short term, but the owner must register the property with the town. State law, A.R.S. 9-500.39, allows short-term rentals in every municipality. The town has dropped its rental license and fees and kept registration. Before registering, an owner needs to:

  • Confirm the property lies inside the town limits, using the town's "Do I live in QC?" map.
  • Get a transaction privilege tax license from the Arizona Department of Revenue, which applies even when the owner books through an online marketplace.
  • Register the rental with the Maricopa County Assessor (602-506-3406) or Pinal County Assessor (520-866-6361) under A.R.S. 33-1902.
  • Provide the parcel number and emergency contact information.

Registration questions go to Development@QueenCreekAZ.gov. An association's rules may be stricter than the town's, so a buyer should read them first.

The town handles permits, zoning, engineering, traffic applications and code enforcement complaints through its Development Nexus online portal. You can search a property's project history there, and 480-358-3003 is the help line. Legitimate permit payment emails come only from DevSvcsNexus@queencreekaz.gov. Payment is made only in the portal by ACH or credit card, and the town never asks for wire transfers.

If you built an addition, patio cover or pool, check the portal for permit records before you list. A missing final inspection is better fixed by you than discovered by a buyer's inspector.

In Maricopa County the standard recording fee is $30 per document. A certified copy costs $1 per page plus $3 per document certification. For a parcel on the Pinal County side, ask the Pinal County Recorder for its current fee.

Each deed that transfers title carries an affidavit signed by buyer and seller, or their agents, under A.R.S. 11-1133. It asks for the price, the parcel number and whether the house will be owner-occupied or rented. The recorder must refuse a deed without a complete affidavit unless the deed bears an exemption notation. Your title or escrow company usually prepares it with the deed.

1. Find your parcel number and confirm the county.
  2. Check the Development Nexus portal for permit records, and fix any missing final inspection.
  3. Collect HOA documents and any unpaid dues statement.
  4. Gather written offers and compare your net from each.
  5. Open escrow so the title company prepares the deed and affidavit.
  6. The deed is recorded in the right county and you receive your proceeds.

A cash buyer can skip the lender's timeline, though the HOA, permit and recording steps still apply.

faqs.q: Is Queen Creek in Maricopa County or Pinal County?
faqs.a: Both. Most of the town is in Maricopa County, and the eastern and southern edges reach into Pinal County. Your parcel number shows which county recorder and assessor apply.

faqs.q: Does Queen Creek require short-term rental registration?
faqs.a: Yes. The town dropped its rental license and fees, but owners still register the property. You need a transaction privilege tax license, the parcel number and an emergency contact. Email Development@QueenCreekAZ.gov with questions.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: The standard fee is $30 per document. A copy costs $1 per page, and certification adds $3 per document. A deed needs the affidavit of property value.

faqs.q: How many people live in Queen Creek?
faqs.a: An estimated 89,770 as of July 1, 2025, up from 59,519 in the 2020 census and 26,361 in 2010.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Queen Creek address?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Most of the Maricopa County part is in Queen Creek Unified, with some areas in Higley Unified and Chandler Unified. The Pinal County part is split among Florence, J. O. Combs and Apache Junction, so ask the district to confirm.
